research.headline: Rare Event Estimation via Iterative Unalignment
research.summary: As agents are deployed with increased autonomy, even extremely rare events along their stochastic output trajectories can occur and prove catastrophic. Safe deployment therefore does not depend on whether these events can occur, but on how often they might. We study the problem of estimating the probability of rare events that arise from stochastic variation in the agent's own actions.

research.headline: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay
research.summary: Modern video games provide a measurable testbed for AI models, combining abilities of visual understanding, instruction decomposition, goal planning, and precise action control over multiple temporal horizons. Existing datasets and benchmarks, however, either cover a narrow range of games, lack language instructions, or rely on high-variance online rollouts. To address these challenges, we introduce GameHorizon, a unified data and evaluation suite that measures gameplay capabilities at different horizons for diverse model families.

research.headline: onPanda: Efficient Annotation of On-Policy Alignment Data for LLMs and Agents via Token-Level Correction
research.summary: We present onPanda, an interactive tool for efficiently annotating LLM alignment data and agent trajectories. onPanda adopts token-level correction as its core interaction: while reading a model response, the annotator locates the first inappropriate token and either picks a substitute from the model's candidate tokens or types the correct text via free-form editing. The system then truncates everything after that position and continues generation from the corrected prefix, repeating this locate-correct-continue loop until a satisfactory response is obtained.

research.headline: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
research.summary: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness.

frontier.headline: Nucleosome simulations suggest mechanisms of electrostatically-driven mesoscale chromatin evolution
frontier.summary: Nucleosomes are structures made up of proteins called histones that bind and compact DNA, driving the mesoscale organization of the chromatin polymer. Although histone proteins have diversified over evolutionary time, their contributions to the corresponding diversification of chromatin structure are poorly understood. Here, we mine protein databases for histones and create \emph{in silico} nucleosomes for 3241 organisms spanning $>$1.5B years of evolution.

frontier.headline: Caffeine disrupts deep sleep even when duration remains normal
frontier.summary: Caffeine can reduce restorative deep sleep, as measured by EEG recordings showing fewer slow brain waves, even for individuals who fall asleep normally and stay in bed for eight hours. Individual sensitivity varies greatly, meaning caffeine consumed earlier in the day may still impact nighttime recovery for some people.

frontier.headline: Analytical framework translates detector sensitivity into stray light requirements
frontier.summary: Researchers present an analytical framework to translate detector sensitivity into stray light requirements for ground-based gravitational wave interferometers. The study derives estimates for various scattering regimes, planar baffles, and deterministic ghost beams intercepted by beam dumps. Applied to Cosmic Explorer, the framework provides conservative design tools for early stray light budgeting in current and future detectors.

frontier.headline: Researchers design quantum Mpemba effect using Stark localization
frontier.summary: Scientists have demonstrated a quantum energy landscape design utilizing Stark localization and localized incoherent hopping that produces the Mpemba effect. Rare detection events trigger hops at rates growing with energy, enabling hotter states to cool faster with super-exponentially separated timescales. This effect is further enhanced by the collective hopping of bound pairs via attractive on-site interactions, with clear signatures accessible in current experimental setups.

frontier.headline: Researchers establish quantitative entropy contraction bounds for finite-dimensional quantum channels
frontier.summary: Quantitative entropy contraction bounds are established for finite-dimensional quantum channels beyond detailed balance. For channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, GNS norm contraction yields relative entropy contraction with a logarithmic dimensional loss. This approach also yields a lower bound on the complete modified logarithmic Sobolev constant for quantum Markov semigroups.

frontier.headline: Improving the CMS High Level Trigger tracking at the HL-LHC with novel and evolved heterogeneous algorithms
frontier.summary: Charged particle track reconstruction is one of the heaviest computational tasks in the event reconstruction chain at LHC experiments. Furthermore, projections for the High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) show that the required computing resources for single-threaded CPU algorithms will exceed those that are expected to be available. It follows that experiments at the HL-LHC will need to employ novel and evolved track reconstruction algorithms, within heterogeneous computing systems that include many-core CPUs as well as GPUs, in the attempt to maximize the computational performance while retaining the best possible reconstruction efficiency.

frontier.headline: Non-Markovian Charging of a Micromaser Quantum Battery
frontier.summary: We theoretically investigate the role played by non-Markovianity in the charging of a quantum battery. We focus on the case of a Micromaser, where the energy is stored in a resonant cavity mode and memory effects are introduced and controlled by coupling this mode to a memory ancilla, described as a two-level system, that in turn sequentially interacts with a stream of two-level chargers through pairwise exchange interactions leading to a partial swap. Through numerical analysis, we show that non-Markovian memory effects act as a resource that enhances both the charging capacity and the stability of this device with respect to the Markovian counterpart.

frontier.headline: Hyperbolic Restricted Boltzmann Machine Neural Quantum State
frontier.summary: We construct the first type of non-Euclidean non-autoregressive neural quantum state (NQS) in the form of the hyperbolic Restricted Boltzmann Machine (HRBM), which is studied in the variational Monte-Carlo (VMC) setting of the Quantum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (QSK) model whose ground state exhibits volume-law entanglement. Across a 512-fold increase in the Hilbert space dimension corresponding to a system size increase from $N=14$ to $N=24$, HRBM NQS robustly outperforms its Euclidean version, the RBM NQS, in terms of better ground state energy optimization as well as lower Renyi-2 $S_2$ and von Neumann $S_{vN}$ absolute entanglement entropy reconstruction errors. More importantly, for all QSK system sizes, HRBM NQS demonstrates a superior expressivity in faithfully reproducing the entire entanglement spectrum of the QSK model from the top eigenvalues down to the tail end across 15 orders of magnitude, while RBM NQS consistently overestimates the sub-dominant modes.

But now, thanks to a timely reallocation of his father’s money , he’s set to be one of the biggest news-media moguls in American history. Having already taken control of CBS News—with little to show for it audience-wise but plenty ideologically —he seems clear to add CNN to his roster of outlets.

voices.headline: The Curious Left-Wing Argument Against New AI Regulations
voices.summary: ET on September 21, 2026 D onald Trump has reacted to terrifying calls for regulation from inside the AI industry with predictable skepticism— insisting , questionably, that the solution requires nothing more than having a “High IQ” president, and further asserting, even more questionably, that he qualifies as one. A more surprising flank of opposition has arisen from a different source: the populist left, which has suggested that existing regulations would be perfectly adequate to rein in a rogue superintelligence bent on eliminating the human race. An article in The American Prospect by Whitney Curry Wimbish and David Dayen, headlined “Congressional Democrats in Hysterics About Saving the World From AI,” argues that the danger from runaway AI is overblown and that no new laws are needed to contain it.

voices.headline: How to Regulate the Ghosts
voices.summary: Ghostbusters is a movie about friendship and slime and the specific melting point of giant marshmallows—which makes it easy to forget that it’s also a movie about regulation. The catastrophe at its center begins when Walter Peck (William Atherton), a bureaucrat from the Environmental Protection Agency, visits the basement of the Ghostbusters’ headquarters and finds a machine he does not understand. The nerdy scientist Egon Spengler (Harold Ramis) explains that it’s a containment system; shutting it off would be “like dropping a bomb on the city.” Peck doesn’t believe in ghosts, and he sure doesn’t believe in the Ghostbusters, so he orders an electrician to turn the machine off.
